#8065. Best 'Mister Rogers' Neighborhood' Songs: 9 Fred Rogers Classics

The anthems of Mister Rogers'might not be ones that make you bust out your lighter, but then again, maybe you should?

Fred Rogers was so good at so many things — rocking a cardigan, controlling puppets, speaking very straightforwardly to children— that it often obscures another skill: he was a damn fine musician, writing a performing hundreds of songs during the show’s masterful run. Figuring out the best Mister Rogers’ songs is mostly all about thinking about why the series was so successful to begin with. Part of the reason why a piece of kids’ entertainment stands the test of time is nearly always connected to music. The reason we still love Sleeping Beauty is because of the brilliant way Disney adapted the classic ballet by Tchaikovsky and, essentially, turned that music into a bunch of pop songs. Nobody thinks about it, but the great visuals in kids’ entertainment are almost always not the reason something is amazing.

The same is true for Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood, to an extent. Yes, we love Fred Rogers’ style, but arguably, the words he spoke and the songs are the real reason the show is so enduring. Contemporarily, the descendant of Mister Rogers; Daniel Tiger’s Neighborhood, also finds its way into the hearts and minds of children through the helpful songs. And though I think some of the Daniel Tiger songs are great, it’s hard to top the originals from Fred himself.

Here are nine songs from Fred Rogers, ranked in order of how memorable and how good they will make you feel.

I call this one the Mister Rogers version of the ’80s anthem “Relax.” Same energy. Same vibe. But, I think Fred Rogers does this concept better than Frankie Goes to Hollywood, don’t you?

Chances are if you’ve heard this song, you remember it from the very famous speech Mister Rogers gave when he addressed the U.S. Senate. Because this is one of his famous songs that deals with complicated feelings, it’s obviously one of his best. It’s a bit of a talking-through-it song, which is like the Rogers version of Bob Dylan impression, except every word is impeccably enunciated.

There’s a Daniel Tiger song called “We Are Friends.” My daughter likes it a lot. But, the thing is, this song is way better.

I have a very strong memory of this song, and I imagine kids who grew up in the ’80s are with me. There’s something about the sentiment of it, combined with the sweetness that really, really stick in your mind. The truth will make you free! He’s right, obviously, but there’s something more magical about it than just that. He’s right, and if you sing along, you can be forgiven for whatever stupid little kid stuff you did. Magic.

If Mister Rogers was Taylor Swift this would be his biggest hit single. This song is great for kids who have just learned the word “fancy,” but also for adults who need to think about their inner-fanciness. A song that is equally good for right before bedtime with your kids, or a boozy brunch with your buddies.

Once we start getting into the top of this list, the songs are basically great because they are absurdly sweet. Still, the message of this one has some intelligence behind it. And, I suspect Paul McCartney wished he’d written it.

Feeling safe is probably the most important thing for a child. The reason why Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood worked so well is that the idea of security and comfort was built into everything about the series. And this song is the musical version of that philosophy.

You know this one by heart. You’re humming it right now. Not just one of the best Mister Rogers songs of all time, but probably one of the best children’s songs, period. Plus, the bass player is taking it for a walk.

The theme song of a TV show is usually memorable in connection with that show and, therefore, hard to really care about in another context. Like, the theme for Knight Rider; you can’t hear it without thinking about David Hasselhoff, several buttons unbuttoned on a shirt, and a talking car. “Won’t You Be My Neighbor” is like that for Fred Rogers. If you hear you, can picture him taking off his shoes, meticulously. And the reverse works, too. If you take your shoes off slowly and calmly, you’ll be humming this tune.

This article was originally published on Oct. 25, 2019

#8064. Top Terrarium Kits for Kids: Fun, Creative, and Educational

Gone are the days of arts and crafts sets that simply involve painting a range of suncatchers to hang up in the window or arranging a fall wreath using pieces of foam leaves because the art of the terrarium kit has fully caught steam this year! Terrarium kits are an engaging way for your kid to experience an easily digestible dose of science mixed with using their own sense of creativity in an activity that doesn't involve a ton of fuss or mess.

The really cool thing about terrarium kits for kids is that there's plenty of variety that can appeal to your child's other interests. For instance, if you have a kid who just loves the idea of cultivating green life on their own, there are ones geared towards creating a cozy den for your seedlings and adding some decorative items for a bit of interest. If your child has always loved heading to your local Natural History Museum to spend a few hours browsing all the dinosaur exhibits, there are terrarium kits that integrate making a miniature dinosaur habitat. To find the coolest terrarium kit for your kid that's going to get them excited, keep reading!

Get ready to inspire the next generation of innovators with these must-have STEM gifts!

According to PBS.org, a terrarium is a "micro-environment" where moisture typically evaporates, condensates, and can fall back down similar to rain, in an enclosed glass container. Every terrarium kit for kids will come with different guidelines depending on the theme and what it has to offer, as there are some terrarium kits for kids that are more geared towards engaging in their artistic sense and giving kids the tools to build their own micro-ecosystem with things like rainbow sand, colored pebbles, moss, and miniature unicorns. It really depends on your child's tastes, abilities, and what gets them excited when it comes to this hands-on activity, because there really is a terrarium kit out there for everyone.

Science experiment kits often contain plenty of items to perform over ten or more experiments. Here are the best science experiment kits for kids.

For some parents, it can feel difficult to gauge what science or craft kit is going to be right for them because there's an abundance of choice. If you need a little help trying to decide on the best terrarium kit for your child, here are a few pointers.

Whenever you're considering a STEM-related kit or an arts and craft activity for your children, it's always best to check out the suggested manufacturer's age because they've worked out what should be an age-appropriate activity for kids based on their skill set and abilities. You always want to be sure that your kid is getting hands-on with an activity that's safe and doesn't include any materials or parts that may pose a problem for their safety.

One of the hardest parts when it comes to terrarium kits for kids is picking out the right one for your child, which hopefully causes a few squeals of delight when they open it. It's always a good idea to think about their interests and passions and move forward from there. For instance, if your kid isn't that interested in growing things but will likely appreciate the artistic aspect of their own terrarium, you may want to opt for a mermaid or unicorn-themed terrarium that's brightly colored and full of opportunities to use their imagination.

A thoughtful and engaging gift idea for any young kid who loves unicorns, the Laoese Light-Up Unicorn Terrarium Kit gives kids everything they need to create a magical unicorn terrarium with colored sand, preserved moss, a beautiful unicorn figure, and a LED nightlight.

There's something so magical about unicorns, especially when you're a kid who is filled with wonder and curiosity. Perfect for the young person in your life who forever lives in a fantasy land, the Laoese Light-Up Unicorn Terrarium Kit is a hands-on craft kit geared toward kids 6 and older that allows them to create their very own dreamy unicorn terrarium.

Kids are given everything they need to create a unique unicorn terrarium, including three colors of magic sand to line the bottom, two colors of preserved moss that they can shape, and five miniature figures, such as a magic castle and a unicorn. Once they're done, if they want to place their magical creation on their bedside table and use it as a nightlight, they can turn on the LED light and even change the colors each night with the included remote control.

An inspired gift for kids who are interested in science and gardening, the Creativity for Kids Grow 'N Glow Terrarium Kit is a charming STEM project that allows kids to grow chia and wheatgrass seeds and create their own whimsically decorated mini ecosystem.

If you have a child who is continually curious about helping in the garden during the spring and summer months, and you want them to explore their interests, the Creativity for Kids Grow 'N Glow Terrarium Kit gives them a hands-on activity to help bring a little more life into the world. This complete science kit designed for kids 6 and older gives them everything they need to plant and grow organic chia seeds and wheatgrass into its own mini ecosystem.

Beyond catering to their growing seeds, this terrarium kit also includes glowing sand to add some whimsy, as well as glowing miniature garden figurines and river stones for texture. There are also two sheets of stickers included, including glow-in-the-dark stickers. Kids can hold their terrarium up to the light and then watch it glow from their desk during the nighttime hours.

For those who love everything prehistoric, the Blue Marble National Geographic Light-Up Dinosaur Habitat Terrarium includes a detailed guide and the materials needed to build their own dinosaur-filled world complete with rock specimens and ryegrass.

This terrarium kit includes everything your child needs to grow their own mini-garden with a prehistoric look as they get a wide-mouthed terrarium, peat pellet to help grow the ryegrass seeds, colored pebbles and river rock, and some miniature dinosaur figures.

To help set the prehistoric scene even further, this dinosaur habitat terrarium comes with a reversible laminated dinosaur backdrop to allow for a distinct panoramic view. Designed for children between the ages of 5 and 12 years old, the 7July Mermaid Terrarium Craft Kit comes with all the supplies needed to assemble and decorate their own mermaid-themed light-up terrarium.

It really depends on who you ask, but there's often been a link between the magic of what lies deep beneath the ocean's surface and the mythical sea creatures known as mermaids. If you're looking for an inspired gift idea for your child that will allow them to fully tap into their sense of whimsy while also putting their little hands to work, the July7 Mermaid Terrarium Kit makes a great choice.

If your child loves the idea of creating a mermaid habitat that shines with an incandescent glow, there's also a light feature that comes with multiple color options and a remote control they can use to switch things up.

Packed with everything they need to create their own little ocean display, this kit includes a clear jar with a cork-top lid, a few colored sands, decorative corals, seaweed and shells, along with 18 life-like marine animals and creatures.

The Laoese Dinosaur Moon Lamp Terrarium Kit makes a delightful gift idea for young dinosaur enthusiasts as they get everything they need to create a cozy dino habitat with an eye-catching moon lamp to go on top.

Blending imagination with space exploration, the Creativity for Kids Crystal Space Terrarium Kit is a fun STEM kit that gives kids an opportunity to grow their own colorful space crystals in a cozy extraterrestrial den.

For kids who dream about going on their own space mission to discover what's out there, this terrarium kit allows them to conduct their own little science experiment by giving them some cool crystal-growing powder and rocks to see their own colorful 'space' crystals grow in as little as 24 hours.

To personalize their space-themed terrarium, there's also vibrant blue space rocks to line the bottom, moon rocks, and two sheets of stickers, including glow-in-the-dark ones. #8063. 10 Simple Desserts That Look Impressive & Still Feel Special

They look high-effort but we promise they’re not.

Sure, it’d be nice to be the person with the time and energy to make an elaborate chocolate-and-matcha checkerboard loaf cake, or a homemade pavlova piled high with syrupy berries. But in reality, most of us don’t even have time to shower as much as we’d like during the week. So, whether you have a party you need to bring a dish to or you just want a little sweet treat at the end of the day, consider these simple desserts that look impressive but take very few brain cells to actually complete. (We used them all up already, OK?) You won’t even need the oven for most of them.

Cool, creamy layers with a dark chocolate frosting on top? That doesn’t sound bad at all. Princess Pinky Girl’s chocolate eclair cake is an easy icebox cake-style recipe that’ll serve a big group with ease.

This slow-cooker apple-pear crisp from Damn Delicious will make your whole house smell incredible; by the time it’s ready to eat, you’ll be more than ready to plop a scoop of ice cream on top and chow down. The sweet, crispy pecan topping really takes this to the next level.

A Beautiful Plate’s strawberry mascarpone tart is such a beautiful dessert, but surprisingly, the hardest part about making it is just arranging the berry slices on top. And don’t worry, her recipe explains precisely how to lay them out to get that bakery case look.

Averie Cooks’ caramel apple nachos are such a cute idea for a movie night with your kids. They’re ridiculously easy to make and customize with your favorite toppings, but they still feel like an extra-special snack.

Family Fresh Meals is kind of a genius for this hack: Make a simple fresh fruit jam and use it to top a scoop of vanilla ice cream to wow your guests, or just treat yourself. Her recipe is incredibly easy and makes a big batch of jam you can use for all sorts of dishes.

Peach clafoutis is a traditional French dessert, with baked golden edges and a custardy center. A Sweet Thyme’s recipe includes a splash of bourbon and vanilla to deepen the peach flavor, but you’ll be surprised by how easy this showstopper is to make.

With Family Fresh Meals’ recipe, you don’t even have to turn on the oven. You’re literally just whipping together a handful of ingredients, smoothing it into a pie crust, and letting it set in the refrigerator. But nothing makes you feel more like the hostess with the mostest than whipping out a gorgeous pie at the end of dinner.

Ina Garten’s viral brownie pudding has a delicious crust with gooey, fudgy goodness underneath. Feel Good Foodie’s version simplifies the ingredient list, and it’s really just a matter of dumping things into a mixer before baking.

BRB while I become known as the strawberry-mascarpone-tart friend...
